display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DRAFTED, READY, LEASED, CODING, then STATIC_AUDIT, then clean verify
A static failure returns to coding. It is not a verification attempt
The same fingerprint three times escalates like any loop

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deterministic scans on the diff. Seconds. No tokens. Shown to the worker
TODO, FIXME, stubs, empty catch, dead controls, hard-coded records,
fake names outside fixtures, mock imports in product code
Edits to protected tests, skip or only, ts-ignore, as any, eslint-disable
Unreachable files, unused planned fields, missing contract surface
Elision placeholders, unplanned large deletions, out of scope, secrets
A real deferral is TODO of an approved ID, and it appears in the final report
Seeds, fixtures and declared generated paths are excluded
A language with weak AST still gets text and type scans, and says so

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Reject with locations. Repeated identical failures escalate

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Soft findings stay on the receipt for high-risk review:
a tiny diff, complexity far below the rules, branches on visible examples

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The database holds requirements, tasks, checks, results and waivers
Graph compile refuses to publish unless:
every in-scope requirement has a task and a check
every task has a requirement
every rule-bearing requirement has a held-back or generated check
A waiver is low-risk, or the developer approved it
400 edge cases and 320 tasks: publish fails and lists the 80

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The implementing worker does not write the checks
Red before green: a new check must fail on the code before the task
A surviving mutation means the check is too weak
The final audit samples pairs. A Manager asks whether the check
observes the requirement. Disagreement goes to the planner

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Every linked check passed
for this artifact, including in-scope rules?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rejected. Missing checks are listed
A feature stays open until every one of its requirements passes
at the current versions

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Tests are read-only. The verifier runs them
Held-back and generated cases make hard-coding fail
flag_blocked and dispute_test are the cheap honest exits
The worker prompt says: disagree, stop, never special-case
The hint ladder caps retries, because more feedback increases gaming
A Senior review of high-risk diffs is advisory
A detected shortcut lowers that model's pass-rate for the class

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
I fixed it myself runs the same audit
The developer may override a finding, and that override is recorded

svg.text: Static audit and the traceability gate
